I refactored the sorter around subrange support, which removes another whole-array assumption from the API and simplifies the internal structure.

[InsertionSort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/035_insertion_sort/InsertionSort.java:1) now has `sort(...)` and `isSorted(...)` overloads for `fromIndex`/`toIndex` on both `int[]` and generic arrays. The insertion step now respects a lower bound, and range validation is centralized so bounds checks and error messages are consistent. The existing whole-array methods delegate into those range-aware paths.

I updated [InsertionSortDemo.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/035_insertion_sort/InsertionSortDemo.java:8) to show a partial in-place sort, and expanded [InsertionSortSelfTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/035_insertion_sort/InsertionSortSelfTest.java:8) with coverage for partial sorting and partial sortedness on both primitive and generic APIs.
